questions.question: Distinguish between goods and services and classify each as durable, semi-durable or non-durable where it applies: a fridge, a school jersey, bread, a taxi ride. Explain why spending on durable goods changes more in hard times.
questions.expected_answer: Goods are physical products; services are activities performed for someone. Fridge: durable good. School jersey: semi-durable good. Bread: non-durable good. Taxi ride: a service. Households can postpone buying durables, so spending on them falls sharply when incomes fall and rises when incomes grow, while non-durables are bought every week.

questions.question: Use the tomato schedule (price per box / demanded / supplied): R40 500/100; R50 400/200; R60 300/300; R70 200/400; R80 100/500. Identify the equilibrium price and quantity, the surplus or shortage at R70 and at R50, and explain how the market corrects each.
questions.expected_answer: Equilibrium R60, 300 boxes (demand = supply). At R70: surplus of 400 − 200 = 200 boxes; sellers lower prices to sell stock, price falls towards R60. At R50: shortage of 400 − 200 = 200 boxes; buyers compete and offer more, price rises towards R60.

questions.question: Name four consumer rights under the Consumer Protection Act of 2008 and explain the role of the Competition Commission.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: fair and honest dealing; information in plain language, including total price; choice, including cancelling certain agreements and refusing unwanted marketing; safe, good-quality goods with return of defective goods within six months for repair, replacement or refund; fair contract terms; privacy. The Competition Commission (Competition Act 1998) investigates price fixing, market division and abuse of dominance, which raise prices and reduce choice; offenders can be fined.
